en: Oṃ, homage to you, Vajratīkṣṇa, the cutter of suffering, the embodiment of the wisdom of insight, the gnosis-body, the Lord of Speech, Arapacana!

Having visualized oneself as the Blessed One, Siddhaikavīra Mañjuvajra— whose form is like the rays of the autumn moon, holding a blue lotus in the left hand and displaying the gesture of granting boons (*varada*) with the right—
one obtains the speech of Sarasvatī within three weeks, [realizing] the primordially unarisen, naturally luminous, and utterly pure realm of phenomena (*suviśuddhadharmadhātu*).
Within six months, one attains mastery over speech;
one beholds the Blessed Lord Vāgīśvara directly and gains the power of retaining all that has been heard.

For six months, one should drink at dawn half a *tolaka* measure of *vacā*, consecrated one hundred and eight times, with milk, oil, or ghee for one month; thereby dullness, stammering, and muteness are destroyed. One becomes possessed of a voice as sweet as a cuckoo in rut and clear speech.
After six months, the scriptures heard from the sky become manifest to the senses.
What has been heard does not perish; one becomes a possessor of the power of retention. // 39 //
Oṃ, homage to this speech!
This is the heart-mantra of the venerable Lord Vāgīśvara.
Abiding in the previously described meditative absorption and practicing it, one performs all the previously mentioned rites.

Having descended into a great river flowing to the ocean until the water reaches the neck, and having taken one hundred thousand buds of jasmine flowers, one should recite the mantra and cast each bud into the current.
A single bud comes floating up on the stream; if it does not touch the teeth but passes through the throat, one attains the state of being sustained by the *śruti*.
By offering four hundred thousand flowers as they are obtained, one becomes equal to Vāgīśvara.
[The powder] from the bees is two *māṣa* and a quarter in measure.

Having consecrated [the medicine] one hundred and eight times, and having prepared a mandala at dawn, one should worship the Blessed One according to one's means and drink it with clarified butter or sour gruel. Within six months, one becomes a possessor of the Vedas (*śrutidhara*), eloquent, and endowed with a sweet voice. By reciting the king of mantras one hundred thousand times according to the procedure for preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*), it becomes accomplished.
Afterwards, during a lunar or solar eclipse, holding a sword made of native iron in one’s own hand, one should recite the mantra until one sees the moon released.
One becomes a sword-vidyādhara.
In this same way, the wheel, vajra, trident, arrow, mallet, noose, and so forth are to be accomplished.
Having prepared elixirs through mantras and other means, they are to be accomplished.
One should prepare the substances for subjugation by mixing collyrium, *tilaka*, foot-unguents, and other such items.
Having filled a vessel with milk-rice or curd-rice mixed with ghee and sugar, one should hold it with the hand, recite the mantra, and consume it; thus one attains a lifespan of five hundred years.
By placing *māṣa* beans in the mouth and reciting the mantra, sprouts will emerge, and one becomes a poet, a possessor of scriptural knowledge, eloquent, and wise.
By performing one hundred thousand homas with lotuses, the Blessed One becomes manifest.
By performing one hundred thousand homas with wood-apples (*bilva*), one attains sovereignty over the three worlds.
By performing four hundred thousand homas with whatever flowers are available, the perfection of speech (*vāksiddhi*) is attained.

By means of an oblation of five kinds of grain (*pañcavrīhi*) smeared with clarified butter, performed four hundred thousand times, one attracts a *yakṣiṇī* or a maiden from the netherworld (*pātāla*).
This should likewise be done with the five types of sacrificial fuel-sticks (*samidh*).
Through constant practice, even the state of Buddhahood is accomplished in this very life. // 40 //
Oṃ hrīḥ hūṃ.
This king of mantras yields results equal [to those of other practices]. // 41 //
Oṃ hrīḥ, homage to Mahāsarasvatī, the portion of Mahāmāyā.
This is the heart-mantra of the Noble Ārya-Tārā Bhaṭṭārikā, which performs all rites:

*oṃ prakṛtipariśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ prakṛtipariśuddho ’haṃ sabāhyābhyantaram*. Having contemplated that the entire universe, including the moving and the unmoving, as well as oneself, are pure by nature both internally and externally.

There is a white lotus measuring seven cubits in size; upon it is a moon disc, in the center of which is the Blessed Lady, whose two arms are adorned with a lotus and the gesture of granting boons, her form consisting of great compassion, intent on helping others, and delighting in bestowing the accomplishment of the practitioners' desired aims.

Having visualized oneself as Mahāsarasvatī—whose form is like the rays of the autumn moon, whose body is draped in white garments, whose heart is covered by a necklace of white pearls, and whose body is adorned with various jewels; who illuminates the infinite and boundless world-systems with thousands of shimmering rays; who has the appearance of a twelve-year-old, yet whose physical form is graced by the onset of fresh youth—and having visualized before her the goddess Prajñā, to her right Medhā, behind her Mati, and to her left Smṛti, all goddesses beautiful with the aforementioned qualities.

Then, having visualized a white-syllabled *oṃ* in the center of a lunar disc at one's own navel, and contemplating the unceasing stream of the entire multitude of speech emanating from it, the practitioner of mantra, with mind focused exclusively on that and self-restrained, should recite the mantra. Remaining silent, within a month he attains the voice of Sarasvatī, like the sun amidst a ruby;
even a slayer of a Brahmin achieves success in three months.
Within six months, one becomes equal in eloquence to Sarasvatī.
One should drink clarified butter prepared with goat’s milk, abhayā, vyoṣa, pāṭhā, ugrā, śigru, and rock salt, consecrated seven times with mantras. (1)
A wise person should cook one *prastha* of ghee with four times as much milk and medicinal herbs in the measure of one *pala* each, using a slow, gentle fire. (2)
By consuming it for only one month, one attains unsurpassed speech;
through its use for six months, one shall directly attain the state of Lord of Speech. (3)
Speech is perfected by licking a preparation consisting of vacā, yaṣṭyāhva, sindūra, pathyā, nāgara, dīpaka, kuṣṭha, kaṇā, and jīraka. (4)

Having worshipped the Lord of Gods in the morning with fragrant flowers and other offerings, and having consecrated it seven times with mantras, one should consume it; in six months, one will become a retainer of what has been heard. (5)
In three months one becomes eloquent, and in one month one becomes wise;
one attains a sweet voice with the resonance of a intoxicated cuckoo. (6)

At dawn, having consecrated seven *harītakī* fruits from the Himalayas and Himalayan *vacā* with mantras, one should consume them for one month; by that very month, one becomes intelligent, eloquent, pure-voiced, and wise; after six months, one becomes a possessor of the power of retention (*śrutidhara*). // 42 //
Oṃ, O Goddess who speaks with eloquence, restrain my speech, O Sarasvatī, O Great White One; svāhā!
This heart of Mahāśvetāmbujā performs all the aforementioned functions. // 43 //
Oṃ arkamālini kiṇi kiṇi khiṇi khiṇi svāhā!

Having visualized oneself as Mañjuvajra in the form of a youth, with the Blessed One Siddhaikavīra—who is composed of stainless syllables and holds a book in his hand—with the sword of wisdom (*prajñākhaḍga*) in his right hand;
one should then contemplate Arkamālinī Mahāsarasvatī in front, Mahāśrī behind, Keśinī to the right, and Upakeśinī to the left.
One should meditate on them all as having the appearance of autumn moonbeams and being adorned with every ornament.

Thus, remaining in meditative absorption and established in the observances, one should perform worship according to one's means and recite four hundred thousand repetitions of this mantra according to the previously described sequence and the rules for preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*).

Then, having consecrated either *sārasvata* or *brahmī* ghee in a quantity of one *pala*, one should drink it while established in meditative concentration, imagining that it has been given by Sarasvatī herself with her own hand.
In this regard, this is the Brāhmī-ghṛta: one should cook one prastha of ghee with the juice of brāhmī and milk;
and one should add these medicinal herbs to be ground into a paste therein:
haridrā, mālatī, trivṛtā, and harītakī. (7)
The remaining portions of these are known as *karṣas*.

One should take long pepper (*pippalī*), *viḍaṅga* seeds, and rock salt (*saindhava*) combined with sugar; having thoroughly mixed all of this, one should cook it over a mild fire for ten *śaras*. (8)
Then, by merely consuming it, one attains unsurpassed purity of speech;
through practice for seven nights, one becomes equal to the kinnaras. (9)
By using it for only one month, a person shall become possessed of wisdom;
by using it for three months, he shall become a supreme retainer of what has been heard. (10)
Within six months, that person shall become manifest as equal to Vāgīśvara;
he destroys the eighteen types of leprosy and the seven great consumptive diseases. (11) // 44 //
Oṃ, homage to Mañjuśrī, the glory of infinite wisdom.
Having visualized oneself as Vāgīśvara surrounded by the four goddesses previously mentioned, one should recite the mantra according to the sequence stated before;
thus one performs all the rites previously described. // 45 //
Oṃ arapacana dhīḥ svāhā.

Having prepared a mandala in a secluded place and having fully worshipped the Blessed One Vāgīśvara and the venerable Guru, one should sit upon a comfortable seat and generate the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).

Thereafter, having recited three times the mantra "Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature; I am pure by nature," and having contemplated oneself and the entire universe as pure by nature, one should bring forth emptiness before oneself and instantly visualize oneself as being perfectly manifested, white in color, seated upon a moon disc atop a white lotus, holding a sword and a book.
Having visualized oneself as Vāgīśvara, with Keśinī on the right and Upakeśinī on the left— both white in color and holding jewel-lotuses—
one should contemplate [them] in front.

One should visualize Jālinīprabha as white in color, standing upon a solar disc, holding a blue lotus, and with a lunar radiance behind him; one should visualize Candraprabha as standing upon a lunar disc, holding a blue lotus, and with a lunar radiance behind him.

Then, having contemplated the syllable *A* flickering and surrounded by a garland of flames within one's own heart, one should contemplate the wheel produced from it—eight-spoked, adorned with the entirety of speech, and rapidly revolving.
For one who practices in this way, after six months, all treatises, even those not previously heard, become manifest both in meaning and in text.
Within one year, he becomes equal to the Lord of Speech. This is the procedure for the Arapacana wheel. // 46 //
Oṃ Vāgīśvara Muḥ.
By reciting this mantra as before, the previously mentioned results are attained.
In the center of the wheel, the syllable *muḥ* should be visualized as surrounded by garlands of flames.
This is the procedure for the Wheel of Wisdom (*prajñācakra*). // 47 //
Oṃ dharmadhātuvāgīśvara muḥ svāhā.

Having meditated upon the self as consisting of five elements according to the previously described sequence, one should contemplate a sixteen-spoked wheel containing the syllable *muḥ* at its center; or for those contemplating an eight-spoked wheel, the aforementioned fruits arise. // 48 //
Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa-varada muḥ svāhā.

Having instantly visualized oneself as the solitary hero Vāgīśvara, an effulgent mass of light produced from the syllable *muḥ* that illuminates the circles of the quarters, one should then contemplate a solar disc in one’s own heart produced from the syllable *oṃ*, resplendent with hundreds of thousands of rays and illuminating all world-systems without exception.
By meditating in this manner, the yogi becomes equal to Vāgīśvara within just six months;
the previously mentioned fruits arise for him. Thus it is said.
The third chapter in the *Siddhaikavīramahātantrarāja*.
